title: An active divisor subfamily is epimorphic
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\iota:K\to C$ a monomorphism of abelian sheaves, and $C\simeq\underline{\mathbb Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $g:\bigoplus_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)}j_{A_i!}\underline{\mathbb Z}\to K$ be epi, where $A_i$ are opens and $c_i$ are natural labels [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Suppose its canonical unit images $s_i$ have constant value $c_i$ in $C$. Let $q:\operatorname{Fin}(m)\to\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ be any function. Suppose that at each point in the union of the $A_i$ there is an index $k$ with $x\in A_{q(k)}$ and $c_{q(k)}$ dividing every label active at $x$. For any stalk coordinates $e_x:C_x\simeq\mathbb Z$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], the coproduct map with kth component the q(k)th component of g is epi. No compactness, positivity, injectivity of q, or bound on the labels is required.

source.place: Lemma 0A38, normalized generators and filtration paragraph: retain generators whose active divisor is still present; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A38

proof.text: Define the retained map by Sigma.desc. Sigma.ι_desc shows that its canonical unit sections and their values are inherited from g. Apply the selected-stalk-range formula with the predicate True to g and to the retained family to identify both stalk ranges with their active-label closures.

Every retained active label is an original active label, giving one subgroup containment. For an original active label, use hretain to obtain a retained active divisor. Multiplying that divisor by the integer divisibility witness places the original label in the retained closure. Closure_le proves the reverse containment.

The stalk functor preserves epis, so g is surjective on stalks. The inclusion of K followed by e_x is injective on stalks. The equal ranges therefore imply surjectivity of the retained map on stalks. Its cokernel stalks are zero by preservation of cokernels; detection of zero sheaves by stalks implies the cokernel is zero, and epi_of_isZero_cokernel concludes.

theorem constantSubsheaf_divisor_subfamily_epi
    (X : TopCat.{u}) (K C : Sheaf AddCommGrpCat X) (ι : K ⟶ C) [Mono ι]
    (isoC : C ≅ (constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
      (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
    (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Opens X) (c : Fin n → ℕ)
    (g : (∐ fun i => (abelianOpenExtensionByZero (A i)).obj
      ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A i)))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) ⟶ K)
    (_hg : Epi g)
    (s : ∀ i, K.obj.obj (op (A i)))
    (hsection : ∀ i,
      (Sigma.ι (fun j => (abelianOpenExtensionByZero (A j)).obj
        ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A j)))
          AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) i ≫ g).hom.app
        (op (A i))
        (abelianOpenExtensionSection (A i)
          ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A i)))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (A i) le_rfl
          ((toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A i)))
            ((Functor.const (Opens ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A i)))ᵒᵖ).obj
              (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))).app
            (op ((Opens.map (A i).inclusion').obj (A i))) (ULift.up 1))) = s i)
    (hvalue : ∀ i, (ι ≫ isoC.hom).hom.app (op (A i)) (s i) =
      (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        ((Functor.const (Opens X)ᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))).app
          (op (A i)) (ULift.up (c i : ℤ)))
    (m : ℕ) (q : Fin m → Fin n)
    (hretain : ∀ x : X, x ∈ iSup A →
      ∃ k, x ∈ A (q k) ∧ ∀ j, x ∈ A j → c (q k) ∣ c j)
    (e : ∀ x : X, TopCat.Presheaf.stalk C.obj x ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)) :
    let D := fun i => (abelianOpenExtensionByZero (A i)).obj
      ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj (A i)))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
    Epi (Sigma.desc (fun k ↦ Sigma.ι D (q k) ≫ g))
